newsitem.title: USA: US senator to begin electricity workshops in February.
newsitem.headline: US senator to begin electricity workshops in February.

text.p: U.S. Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, R-Alaska, said Wednesday he planned to hold a series of workshops beginning in late February to debate opening the electricity market to competition.

The first six-hour workshop would focus on state efforts to promote competition, obstacles to competition, the role of public power in a competitive market, and the role of Congress in promoting competition.
"Before we proceed with legislation, we need to foster greater consensus between all parties," Murkowski said in a statement.
"My goal is to assure all consumers the lowest-priced electricity consistent with reliable service," Murkowski said.
Achieving that goal would require "deregulation, regulatory streamlining, and empowering the states to promote retail competition," he said.
Murkowski said the workshops were designed to create more consensus among competing interests.
Reliability of service, taxes, environmental concerns, mergers, holding companies, and independent power contracts were among many issues expected to be raised at the workshops.
